data.title: Duan Yongping: Elon Musk Has Significantly Improved My Quality of Life
data.description:
Duan Yongping said on November 27 that Elon Musk had significantly improved his quality of life, citing his use of a Tesla and Starlink.

According to Odaily, he was responding to a social media user who said they had been an early Tesla customer and sold their Model S only this year. The user proposed a $2 bet: $1 that Tesla’s share price would be lower in 10 years than it is today, and $1 that Apple’s would be higher. Duan said he had neither won nor lost, but had “actually won” because he drives a Tesla and uses Starlink.

data.title: Arthur Hayes: December Fed Meeting to Be Key for Sentiment as Nasdaq and Tech Stocks May Stay Under Pressure
data.description:
Maelstrom Chief Investment Officer Arthur Hayes said the Federal Reserve’s December FOMC meeting would be important for market sentiment. According to Odaily, Hayes expects selling in the Nasdaq and technology stocks to resume, potentially weighing further on Bitcoin.

Hayes said he would look for gold to rise and the Nasdaq to fall. He described the failure of a U.S. bank last Friday as a minor market tremor.

On the possibility of further Fed rate increases, Hayes said he did not mind if markets experienced more pain, as he believes a bailout would eventually follow. He said the key question is how much pain markets must endure before policymakers resume monetary easing. These were his personal market views.

data.title: Chainflip Tracks Attacker and Develops User Fund Recovery Plan
data.description: Chainflip is tracking the attacker and developing a plan to recover user funds. According to Odaily, the team is pursuing on-chain and off-chain leads and designing a recovery fund to be managed through on-chain records and protocol governance. Unpaid loans will be settled at prices in effect when the attack occurred. The stolen BTC has not been moved, and ETH deposited in Tornado Cash may also remain unmoved. Chainflip has reported the incident to relevant law enforcement agencies and is offering a 10% bounty if the attacker returns 90% of the funds. The protocol remains paused and will not restart until its security review and remediation are complete.

data.title: Bank of England Urges Financial Firms to Accelerate Post-Quantum Cryptography Migration
data.description:
The Bank of England urged financial institutions to accelerate migration to post-quantum cryptography to address risks from quantum computing. According to Odaily, the central bank said in its November Financial Stability Report that quantum computing could threaten widely used public-key cryptography, affecting financial transactions, identity authentication and digital signatures. It urged firms to plan migrations early, identify cryptographic dependencies in existing systems and prioritize upgrades to critical operations.

Under the U.K. National Cyber Security Centre’s roadmap, financial institutions should develop migration plans by the end of 2028, complete migrations for high-priority operations by the end of 2031 and migrate other systems by the end of 2035. The Bank of England also said the financial system’s high degree of interconnection means delays by a single institution or third-party provider could amplify systemic risks.

data.title: Thailand Raids Suspected Crypto Exchange Operation in Pattaya With About 200 Million Baht in Monthly Transactions
data.description:
Thai police and Chonburi immigration officials raided a house and an apartment in Pattaya on November 27, arresting six Chinese nationals. According to Odaily, police suspect the group used a USDT exchange business as cover to handle about 200 million baht a month, with some funds possibly linked to scams and online gambling; the victims were mainly in China.

Five Chinese nationals were found conducting USDT exchanges at the house, where officers seized computers, 13 phones, a router and three cryptocurrency hardware wallets. At an apartment in Jomtien, officers arrested another Chinese man, He Yalong, whom investigators suspect of directing the group, and seized two desktop computers and two phones.

Police said the group may have moved illicit funds through transactions related to online shopping. Authorities have not announced specific charges. Chonburi immigration officials will continue tracing the funds and investigating other possible participants. The six detainees will be deported after Thai legal proceedings are completed.

data.title: Arthur Hayes Warns of AI Risks, Sees Crypto Bull Market After Crisis
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher citing The Block, Arthur Hayes discussed the risk of overinvestment in the AI industry and outlined three concerns. Debt spreads for AI hyperscalers are widening, with some nearing levels associated with default risk; he singled out Oracle’s credit default swaps for attention.

Hayes said U.S. President Donald Trump’s involvement in decisions related to Nvidia suggests the U.S. government recognizes the need to rescue the company. He added that monetary authorities would also need to support the response.

Hayes said an “incredible cryptocurrency bull market” could begin after the process is over.

The discussion addressed cybersecurity challenges amid the development of AI.

data.title: AI TRENDS | Leopold Aschenbrenner's Q3 Letter Bets on AI Agents and Superintelligence, Names 10 Potential Beneficiaries
data.description:
Situational Awareness founder Leopold Aschenbrenner said in his third-quarter investor letter that markets are underestimating how quickly AI will advance from chatbots to agents and superintelligence. He projected that 2027 could bring AI advances on a scale equivalent to those of the previous three years.

According to Odaily, Aschenbrenner’s investment focus spans five areas: foundation models, memory chips, GPU rentals, data-center power supply and robotics. He named Anthropic, SK Hynix, Kioxia, SanDisk, SpaceX, Nebius, SharonAI, CoreWeave, IREN and Bloom Energy as 10 companies to watch.

Aschenbrenner also said some software companies, AI-wrapper businesses, chip designers and current AI industry winners could lose competitive advantages as AI gradually replaces engineers, code, intellectual property and management capabilities. He listed Salesforce, Adobe, ServiceNow, C3.ai, Synopsys, Arm, Nvidia, AMD, Broadcom and ASML as companies to approach cautiously. The views are his own and are not definitive market forecasts.

data.title: XRP Holders Seek 31.1 Billion Escrow Burn; David Schwartz Says Validators Cannot Force Ripple
data.description:
Ripple CTO Emeritus David Schwartz said XRP Ledger validators cannot force Ripple to burn its escrowed XRP, even with more than 80% support. A group called Make XRP Great Again urged Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse in an open letter on November 16 to burn 31.1 billion escrowed XRP by March 31, 2027, according to BeInCrypto.

An amendment requires 29 of 35 validator votes and must maintain that support for two weeks before activation. Schwartz said a majority can change its own rules but cannot compel dissenting validators or seize Ripple’s escrow; validators backing a burn amendment would instead isolate themselves from the network. He said in February 2024 that Ripple could mimic a burn by sending escrow releases to an account no one controls. Ripple reported about 31.1 billion XRP and plans to release 1 billion XRP from escrow on December 1. XRP traded near $0.95, down nearly 30% in a month.

data.title: India’s Central Bank Intensifies Scrutiny of $247 Billion Gold-Loan Sector as Prices Fall
data.description:
According to Jin10, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is intensifying scrutiny of the country’s $247 billion gold-loan industry as falling gold prices erode the collateral value lenders require from borrowers. RBI officials have reviewed early indicators of stress, asset quality, and loan amounts relative to pledged gold. Banks and shadow lenders can lend up to 85% of gold’s value, and the RBI has conducted preventive inspections for breaches of that limit, but has found no evidence of violations so far.

Shadow lenders saw signs of borrower stress in the quarter ended September. A revised rule prohibiting interest-payment deferrals also led to higher default rates. Gold prices have fallen 30% since peaking in January, with the decline accelerating in recent weeks amid expectations that the Federal Reserve will take a more hawkish stance.

data.title: Binance Blockchain Week: Industry Leaders Call for "Collective Resilience" as AI Reshapes Crypto Security
data.description:
Security took center stage at Binance Blockchain Week 2026 as industry leaders convened for a panel titled "Collective Resilience: Securing the Digital Asset Industry in the AI Era."
The session brought together Jimmy Su, Chief Security Officer at Binance; Vivek Chudgar, Managing Director JAPAC at Mandiant Consulting, Google; Silvia Ihensekhien, Chief Security Advisor, GCR at Microsoft; and Pooja Saha, Sr. Security & Compliance BD Manager of APJC at AWS. Eowyn Chen, Binance's Chief Marketing Officer, moderated the discussion.
Jimmy Su noted that AI is "changing the economics and the speed of cyber attacks," enabling attackers to bridge knowledge gaps and compress attack timeframes — a particular challenge for crypto's 24/7, largely irreversible transactions.
Guests also discussed AI-enabled tactics — deepfakes, AI-written malware, automated reconnaissance, and LLM-based phishing at scale — citing North Korean groups using AI-generated deepfake video calls to steal over $400 million in crypto over 18 months.
Panelists agreed that while AI changes the scale and speed of attacks, cybersecurity fundamentals remain unchanged. Vivek Chudgar stressed visibility ("if you can't see, you can't stop"), understanding weak signals, and rapid response, urging startups to tightly manage privileged access, avoid architectural "built-in trust," and build telemetry.
Pooja Saha emphasized AWS's shared responsibility model, urging builders to define clear ownership and boundaries for AI agents.
Guests also discussed cross-industry information sharing, noting crypto lacks the coordinated threat intelligence seen in banking and healthcare. Standardization and pre-built trust protocols were flagged as critical.
Jimmy Su outlined Binance's three-pronged transformation: asset-centric security, containment to limit blast radius, and rapid response. He called for a shift "from individual security to collective resilience," envisioning collective intelligence where a hack detected by one company reaches collaborators within seconds.
Chen summarized the takeaway: design with zero trust, but "for our industry to move forward, we need to build a trust protocol."

data.title: Franklin Templeton VP Says Banks Are Pivoting to Institutional Wallets
data.description:
Binance announced on X that Emilio Anting, Vice President of Digital Asset Partnerships at Franklin Templeton, said, “We believe the world's moving from an account based ecosystem into a wallet based ecosystem.”

Anting added, “I'd say in the last 12 months we've seen a lot of the TradFi firms, especially the big banks, now really pivot towards bringing in institutional wallet infrastructure for institutional clients.”

data.title: Vitalik: EIP-8037 Complaints Are Reasonable; Glamsterdam Should Not Be Rushed
data.description: Vitalik said complaints about EIP-8037 causing some contracts to fail are reasonable. According to Odaily, Ethereum should not establish a security norm advising applications to maintain centralized upgrade backdoors. He said core developers have a responsibility to support applications affected when a fork changes protocol features they reasonably considered stable, and that this support should continue and be strengthened. Given Glamsterdam’s disruptive nature, he said it should not be rushed.

data.title: STOCKS | Gulf IPO Activity Slows Sharply as Geopolitical Risks Rise
data.description: According to Jin10, Bahrain-based investment bank SICO said Gulf IPO activity had slowed sharply this year amid rising geopolitical uncertainty. Six IPOs have raised about $1.5 billion year to date, with most of the proceeds raised in the first quarter. The region recorded 18 IPOs in 2025 and 23 in 2024. Foreign outflows from Gulf stock markets have reached about $2 billion this year, while the S&P GCC Index, which tracks stocks across Gulf Cooperation Council markets, has fallen 1.2%. SICO expects regional stock markets to remain volatile as investors seek clearer signals on geopolitical risks, interest rates, and the timing of government projects.
